findings.explanation: The example wires google_kms_crypto_key.static into the module's boot_disk.kms_key_self_link (via var.kms_key_self_link), but no google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member/_binding anywhere in the repo grants roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter to the Compute Engine service agent (service-PROJECT_NUMBER@compute-system.iam.gserviceaccount.com). GCP requires this grant before the Compute Engine API will create a CMEK-encrypted boot disk — without it, `terraform apply` fails with a permission-denied error at disk-creation time, even though the HCL for the key and the boot_disk block are both individually correct. This is a GCP platform requirement verified independently of holden's engine (not something a deterministic scan confirmed) — holden's existing HLD_GCP_092 only checks that kms_key_self_link is set (not_null) and cannot see this at all, and an attempted requires_companion/linked_via policy to detect it turned out not to fire on real HCL either; see suggested_policies below for why.
findings.title: CMEK boot disk has no IAM grant for the Compute Engine service agent — apply will fail

findings.explanation: confidential_instance_config.enable_confidential_compute = true is hard-coded, but var.machine_type defaults to e2-micro. Confidential VMs (AMD SEV) only run on N2D, C2D, C3D (and TDX on C3); the E2 series is not supported, so the Compute API rejects the instance at apply time with the module's defaults. Plan succeeds, so nothing catches this before apply. Principle is a best fit: an apply-time correctness bug.
findings.remediation: Default machine_type to a Confidential-capable series (e.g. n2d-standard-2) and add a lifecycle precondition that rejects incompatible series while confidential compute is on, or make confidential compute a variable.
findings.resolution: machine_type default changed to n2d-standard-2; lifecycle precondition rejects non-Confidential series.
findings.title: Confidential Computing is enabled but the default machine_type e2-micro does not support it

findings.explanation: google_compute_network.this sets auto_create_subnetworks = false and the example declares no google_compute_subnetwork. The module's network_interface only sets network, and a custom-mode VPC with no subnet cannot host an instance, so apply fails. The module offers no subnetwork variable, so even a caller with subnets cannot pick one in a custom-mode VPC with several regions.
findings.remediation: Add a required subnetwork variable to the module, pass it to network_interface.subnetwork, and add a google_compute_subnetwork (private_ip_google_access, flow logs) in the example's region.
findings.resolution: Added required var.subnetwork wired to network_interface.subnetwork; example adds google_compute_subnetwork.this (PGA + flow logs).
findings.title: Example VPC is custom-mode with no subnetwork, and the module has no subnetwork input — instance creation fails

findings.explanation: The boot disk is zonal in us-central1-a, while the key ring (and so google_kms_crypto_key.static) lives in europe-west1. Compute Engine requires the CMEK key to be in the disk's region (or global/a covering multi-region), so disk creation is rejected. Medium confidence: depends on Compute's location rules, not visible in the HCL.
findings.remediation: Put the key ring in us-central1 (the region of var.zone).
findings.resolution: Example key ring moved to us-central1.
findings.title: Example CMEK key ring is in europe-west1 but the boot disk is in us-central1

findings.explanation: module.staticip receives kms_key_self_link = google_kms_crypto_key.static.id, which depends only on the key. Nothing makes the instance wait for google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.compute_engine, so Terraform may create the CMEK boot disk in parallel with (or before) the grant and fail with permission denied on a fresh apply. The fix for HOLDEN_AI_001 added the grant but not the ordering.
findings.remediation: Reference the key through the IAM member so the dependency is implicit.
findings.title: Instance creation is not ordered after the Compute service agent's KMS grant

findings.explanation: boot_disk.initialize_params.image takes data.google_compute_image.debian.self_link, which resolves to the newest image in the family on every plan. initialize_params.image forces replacement, so each Debian image release plans to destroy and recreate the instance (and its boot disk). With deletion_protection = true the apply then errors, leaving the stack unappliable until someone intervenes.
findings.remediation: Add lifecycle { ignore_changes = [boot_disk[0].initialize_params[0].image] } so the image is only chosen at creation; patch the running VM in-guest.
findings.title: Image family lookup feeds a ForceNew attribute — every new Debian image plans a replacement, which deletion_protection then blocks

findings.explanation: The validation is var.network != "default", but the variable accepts a self_link, so projects/p/global/networks/default or the full https URL to the default network passes and the instance lands on the default VPC (with its permissive default firewall rules). holden's HLD_GCP_091 returns UNKNOWN here because network is a variable.
findings.remediation: Reject any value whose last path segment is default.
findings.resolution: network validation now rejects any value ending in /default.
findings.title: network validation only rejects the literal "default"; a self_link to the default VPC passes

findings.explanation: var.address_type allows INTERNAL, yet the instance always places google_compute_address.static.address in access_config.nat_ip, which only accepts an EXTERNAL address. An INTERNAL address also needs a subnetwork, which the address resource never sets. Any caller choosing INTERNAL gets an apply failure.
findings.remediation: When INTERNAL, reserve the address in var.subnetwork and set network_interface.network_ip instead of creating an access_config; only add access_config.nat_ip for EXTERNAL.
findings.resolution: INTERNAL addresses are reserved in var.subnetwork and set as network_ip; access_config is only created for EXTERNAL.
findings.title: address_type = INTERNAL is accepted but the address is always used as an external NAT IP

findings.explanation: google_compute_address.static sets no region, so it takes the provider's default region. If that differs from the region of var.zone the external address cannot be attached as nat_ip; if the provider has no region (as in the example's provider block) plan depends on ambient gcloud config. The instance and the address should derive their location from the same input.
findings.title: Static address region is not tied to the instance's zone

findings.explanation: google_service_account.instance uses var.name as account_id, which must be 6-30 characters matching ^[a-z](?:[-a-z0-9]{4,28}[a-z0-9])$. The validation accepts anything non-empty, so names like vm, my_vm or a 40-character name pass plan and fail at apply after the address may already exist.
findings.remediation: Validate var.name against the account_id pattern.
findings.resolution: var.name validated against the service account account_id pattern.
findings.title: var.name is also the service account account_id, but validation only checks it is non-empty

findings.explanation: The default scopes are logging.write and monitoring, but scopes only cap what the SA may do; the dedicated SA has no IAM roles at all. Without roles/logging.logWriter and roles/monitoring.metricWriter the Ops Agent's writes are denied, so the instance produces no guest logs or metrics, silently.
findings.remediation: Grant roles/logging.logWriter and roles/monitoring.metricWriter to the SA on the project (togglable), matching the default scopes.
findings.resolution: Added google_project_iam_member.ops granting logWriter/metricWriter, toggled by var.grant_ops_roles (default true).
findings.title: Instance SA gets logging/monitoring scopes but no logWriter/metricWriter roles, so guest logs and metrics are dropped

findings.explanation: The description says CSEK, but the value is a Cloud KMS key (CMEK); CSEK is a raw key supplied in disk_encryption_key_raw. A key resource ID is not a secret, and sensitive = true hides key changes in plan output, which is exactly the diff a reviewer needs to see (changing it replaces the boot disk).
findings.fix: description = "Cloud KMS key (CMEK) self link or ID used to encrypt the boot disk. Required."
findings.remediation: Describe it as a CMEK key and drop sensitive = true.
findings.resolution: Description corrected to CMEK; sensitive removed.
findings.title: kms_key_self_link is documented as CSEK and marked sensitive

findings.explanation: The module's purpose is reserving a static IP and attaching it, but callers cannot read the address (or its self_link) without a data lookup, e.g. for DNS records or firewall allow-lists.
findings.title: Module does not output the reserved static IP address

findings.explanation: The data source reads var.image["family"] and var.image["project"], but the type is map(any) and the validation only checks length > 0, so a map missing either key fails with an index error inside the data source instead of a clear variable error.
findings.fix: type        = object({ family = string, project = string })
findings.remediation: Type it as object({ family = string, project = string }).
findings.title: var.image is map(any) instead of an object with family and project

findings.explanation: rotation_period = "100000s" creates a new key version roughly daily, about 330 billed active versions a year, all retained because old versions must stay enabled to decrypt existing disks. A 90-day period meets common rotation guidance at a fraction of the cost.
findings.resolution: Example rotation_period set to 7776000s (90 days); destroy_scheduled_duration 2592000s also added for HLD_GCP_547.
findings.title: Example KMS key rotates every ~28 hours

findings.explanation: policies lists .holden\policies; on macOS/Linux the backslash is a literal character, so the directory never resolves and local policies are not loaded. There is no scan_roots, so a bare holden scan errors and the example dir is never scanned by default. The only local policy, HLD_PROPOSED_002, also duplicates built-in HLD_GCP_094 and uses the reserved HLD_ prefix.
findings.remediation: Use .holden/policies, add scan_roots for . and example/examplea, and remove the superseded HLD_PROPOSED_002 file.
findings.resolution: .holden.yaml uses .holden/policies with scan_roots; superseded HLD_PROPOSED_002 policy file removed (built-in HLD_GCP_094).
findings.title: .holden.yaml uses a Windows path for local policies and has no scan_roots

suggested_policies.dsl_extension_note: requires_companion.linked_via needs a way to join two resources on "reference the same target resource", not just "resolved attribute values are deepEqual" — the latter fails whenever the joined attribute is a reference to another resource's computed attribute (.id, .self_link, etc.), since holden's resolver correctly marks those graph.DynamicValue (HCL-only, no plan/state access). A fix likely means a graph.Edges-based join instead: for subject r matching LinkedVia.From via an outbound reference edge to target T, require some companion of Type with an outbound reference edge (via LinkedVia.To or similar) to that same T — analogous to what checkRequiresOrderedCompanion already does for its ordering check (matching on shared edge targets, see evaluator.go's OrderedCompanionCheck doc comment, which literally names this same KMS/service-agent pattern as its motivating example), but without requiring an explicit depends_on edge between subject and companion. This is a resolver/graph-matching design decision, not a quick DSL field addition, and it likely explains why HLD_GCP_280 (the existing linked_via precedent) doesn't fire on realistic HCL either — worth verifying and fixing there before this policy is viable.
suggested_policies.rationale: HLD_GCP_092 (GCE instance boot disk must use a customer-managed encryption key) only checks kms_key_self_link not_null and never verifies the companion IAM grant that actually makes CMEK work — the same gap exists in HLD_GCP_101 (Cloud SQL CMEK) and HLD_GCP_285 (GKE node pool boot disk CMEK), which document the grant in remediation prose but don't enforce it either. HLD_GCP_280 (Pub/Sub DLQ service-agent IAM) looks like a precedent for the requires_companion + linked_via + where shape needed here, and the YAML below mirrors it structurally. HOWEVER: built and fixture-tested against a fresh build of current holden HEAD (not the ~2-day-stale system binary I first validated against), this does NOT fire — and neither does HLD_GCP_280 itself, on an equivalent realistic fixture (google_pubsub_subscription with a dead_letter_policy referencing a topic via .id, no companion IAM member — HLD_GCP_280 stayed silent). Root cause: linked_via compares resolved attribute VALUES, but holden's resolver substitutes graph.DynamicValue for any reference to another resource's computed attribute (e.g. `.id`) — the standard, idiomatic way to write this in Terraform — so both sides of the join hit checkCompanion's early-exit Unknown guard before ever comparing. evaluator_test.go's TestEvaluator_LinkedVia only proves the join logic works because it constructs the graph directly in Go with matching plain-string literals ("google_pubsub_topic.dlq" on both sides), bypassing the HCL parser and graph.ResolveAll entirely — it never exercises a real `.id` reference through resolution. This looks like it silently affects every shipped policy using linked_via against a computed-attribute reference, not just this proposal — flagging as requires_dsl_extension since fixing it is a resolver-level design decision (how/whether to resolve or edge-compose cross-resource .id references), not a one-sitting DSL addition.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_003
name: GCE instance boot disk CMEK requires Compute Engine service-agent IAM grant
principle: encryption
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  A google_compute_instance boot_disk with kms_key_self_link set is silently
  broken unless the Compute Engine service agent
  (service-PROJECT_NUMBER@compute-system.iam.gserviceaccount.com) holds
  roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on that key. Terraform does not
  create this IAM binding automatically; without it, disk creation fails at
  apply time with a permission-denied error from the Compute Engine API,
  even though the boot disk's CMEK configuration looks complete in the HCL.
remediation: |
  Grant the Compute Engine service agent decrypt/encrypt access on the key:

  ```hcl
  data "google_project" "current" {
    project_id = var.project
  }

  resource "google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member" "compute_engine" {
    crypto_key_id = google_kms_crypto_key.vm.id
    role          = "roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter"
    member        = "serviceAccount:service-${data.google_project.current.number}@compute-system.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_compute_instance:
    filter:
      path: boot_disk.kms_key_self_link
      not_null: true
    requires_companion:
      type: google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member
      linked_via:
        from: boot_disk.kms_key_self_link
        to: crypto_key_id
      where:
        path: role
        equals: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter

suggested_policies.rationale: Confidential VMs only run on specific machine series (N2D, C2D, C3D for SEV; C3 for TDX; A3). A google_compute_instance with enable_confidential_compute = true on any other series (e.g. e2-micro) passes plan and fails at apply. This is a single-resource attribute check holden can do deterministically.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: LOCAL_GCP_001
name: Confidential GCE instances must use a Confidential-capable machine series
principle: reliability
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  Confidential Computing is only supported on N2D, C2D and C3D (AMD SEV),
  C3 (Intel TDX) and A3 machine series. Enabling it on another series such
  as E2 passes terraform plan but the Compute API rejects the instance at
  apply time.
message: |
  google_compute_instance enables confidential compute on a machine_type
  that does not support it.
remediation: |
  Use a supported series, e.g. machine_type = "n2d-standard-2", or disable
  confidential_instance_config.enable_confidential_compute.
resources:
  google_compute_instance:
    if_equals:
      path: confidential_instance_config.enable_confidential_compute
      value: true
      then:
        path: machine_type
        matches: "^(n2d|c2d|c3d|c3|a3)-"
